answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with unique storage vaults: each identity is assigned one encrypted shard that only it can open, kept like a lantern in a sealed vault. Peers whisper a random byte range, and the identity must return those bytes within seconds, proving it really holds its shard. A farm cannot share one copy across thousands of fakes, because every shard is encrypted under a different key, so ten thousand fakes must pay for ten thousand vaults of storage and bandwidth. One honest agent keeps a single shard cheaply and answers its check once.
